To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variance of virtual performance and the derivative of the virtual mean with respect to the time at which the event occurs can provide important information about the system under investigation, that the difference-based variance and derivative estimations can be effective, and that the modified k-fold cross validation can help tune the parameter k for these estimators.
the variance and derivative estimator of a virtual statistic are unbiased and consistent, and that the variance estimator can be tuned by a modified K-fold method.
the variance and the derivative of virtual performance are useful measures that can be estimated with small-sample bias and variance that are comparable to those of the mean of virtual waiting time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the variance and the derivative of virtual performance, and the development of methods for their estimation, and for tuning the parameters of the variance estimators.
the estimation of virtual performance, and we propose new variance and derivative estimator for virtual performance.
the statistical estimation of virtual performance, and its variance and derivative, and the development of tuning methods for these estimators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the virtual performance, the variance and derivative estimator are useful tools that can provide information not apparent from the mean.
, in the context of simulation analysis, the derivative of virtual performance is a more useful measure of the performance of a system than the variance.
, for virtual performance, the variance and derivative estimator are more accurate than the mean, and the mean is more stable than both the variance and derivative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the presence of a time trend, the variance and derivative estimator are more efficient than the mean estimator, and the mean, variance and derivative estimations are all necessary for a complete understanding of virtual performance.
the derivative estimator has better performance in terms of bias and mean-squared error than the difference-based variance estimators.
the variance estimator is robust, while the derivative estimator is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean, variance, and derivative of virtual performance are all important and useful measures in simulation analytics.
the variance and derivative of virtual performance can be estimated with reasonable precision, even with a relatively small sample.
, in addition to the mean, the variance of virtual performance should also be considered for the analysis of virtual performance.
